summary.title: Computer Graphics from Scratch – Introduction
summary.one_liner: Learn how 3D scenes are rendered by building a software raytracer and a rasterizer from scratch, using only a PutPixel primitive and simple math.
takeaways: The book builds two complete renderers, a raytracer and a rasterizer, from only a method that sets pixel colors.
It uses informal pseudocode and links to working JavaScript implementations that run in a web browser.
Math needed is modest: high-school trigonometry plus a practical linear algebra appendix.
Understanding rendering theory helps when writing GPU shaders, which are software run on GPU hardware.
summary.summary: This is the introduction to Gabriel Gambetta's free online book on computer graphics. It explains that the book focuses only on rendering 3D scenes and is written to be accessible to high-school students while remaining rigorous for professionals. The book is organized into two parts, Raytracing and Rasterization, covering lines, triangles, shading, perspective projection, clipping, hidden surface removal, and textures, with a linear algebra appendix. It uses no existing graphics APIs such as OpenGL or Vulkan, and provides pseudocode plus JavaScript implementations.
